newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina corn condition ratings fall.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina corn condition ratings fall.

text.p: A lack of adequate soil moisture caused the corn crop in North Carolina to deteriorate in the week ended July 13, said the state's agricultural statistics service in its weekly crop update.
"Unfortunately, the lack of rain has several areas of the state drier than farmers would like," the report said.

Soybeans were 96 percent planted as of Sunday, above the five-year average of 95. The crop was rated one percent very poor, two percent poor, 34 percent fair, 56 percent good and two percent excellent.

Sixty percent of the corn crop was silking, below the five-year average of 80 percent. Corn was rated eleven percent very poor, 11 percent poor, 37 percent fair, 40 percent good and one percent excellent.
Soil moisture was rated 18 percent very short, 30 percent short, 50 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
